::: {.kw-overview}
Donor utilisation opens this issue: the US-derived Equitable Donor Assessment Model holds its calibration when tested on almost 26,000 deceased-donor transplants from the UK Transplant Registry, and a 24-year single-centre series shows that dual transplantation of marginal adult kidneys outlasts single high-KDPI grafts even as allocation changes have nearly eliminated the practice. On the perioperative side, a three-centre US experience of 671 robotic transplants, mostly in obese recipients, reports a conversion rate below 1% and acceptable five-year survival. For immunosuppression, a US registry analysis links basiliximab-type induction in steroid-free regimens to more graft loss than thymoglobulin. Two papers temper assumptions about immunological risk: a systematic review finds that randomised data do not show eculizumab prophylaxis reduces antibody-mediated rejection in desensitised recipients, and a Basel cohort finds no sign that red-cell transfusion after transplantation broadens HLA sensitisation. On infection, a multicentre cohort ties recent co-trimoxazole prophylaxis to resistance in ESBL bloodstream isolates, and in living donation a Korean national cohort suggests that a steep post-donation rise in donor blood pressure foreshadows hypertension and faster eGFR loss in the paired recipient.
:::

### 1. [External Validation and Transportability of the Equitable Donor Assessment Model in a National UK Kidney Transplant Cohort.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ekir.2026.107127)
[Ali H, Ahmed O, ElHafeez SA, Murea M, Fülöp T. *Kidney Int Rep*, 2026. PMID: 43022336.]{.kw-ref}

The Equitable Donor Assessment Model (EDAM) uses donor characteristics alone to estimate graft failure while treating death with a functioning graft as a competing event, and it was developed on US data. This research letter, for which the full text was available, applied it to UK Transplant Registry data on adult deceased-donor kidney-only transplants performed from 2012 to 2024, with 25,988 recipients analysable after exclusions for missing data (mainly donor creatinine). Discrimination was moderate, with a concordance index of 0.65, but calibration was close to ideal (intercept 0.003, slope 1.02), and the result barely changed when multiple imputation brought the sample to 27,205. Ten-year graft failure rose steadily across risk bands, from roughly 18% for donors scoring below 0.80 to roughly 28% for those at 0.90 or above, and the curves never crossed. In an exploratory comparison with the UK Kidney Donor Risk Index among 10,288 transplants from 2020 onward, the two tools put 56.1% of kidneys in the same category; most disagreement was in the middle bands, with half of UK-KDRI D2 kidneys rated lowest risk by EDAM, whereas 84.9% of the highest EDAM band were D4 kidneys. Five-year graft failure at the low- and high-risk extremes was almost identical under both systems. Proteinuria was not recorded in the registry and some donor comorbidity fields had to be coded as unknown. The authors stress that the comparison does not show either tool to be superior; for UK practice, the result is a well-calibrated alternative view of donor risk that could be tested in offer-acceptance and longevity-matching simulations before any role in allocation is considered.

### 2. [Long-Term Outcomes With 100 Dual Kidney Transplants From Adult Deceased Donors: Negative Effect of Changes in Kidney Allocation.](https://doi.org/10.1111/ctr.70736)
[Cabrales A, Kumar R, Orlando G, Webb C, McCracken E, Jay CL, Farney AC, Stratta RJ. *Clin Transplant*, 2026. PMID: 42993184.]{.kw-ref}

This single-centre US review covers 100 dual kidney transplants from adult deceased donors with limited nephron mass over 24 years. Recipients were deliberately chosen to be at low immunological risk and with modest nephron requirements (older, smaller, first transplant), and all received antibody induction with tacrolimus, mycophenolate and steroids. The donors had a mean KDPI of 85%, 88% of kidney pairs were machine perfused, 45% were imported, and the first kidney's cold ischaemia averaged 26.8 hours. Delayed graft function affected 28% of recipients, including two cases of primary non-function, and mean GFR at one year was 55 mL/min/1.73 m². Seventy-nine recipients have been followed for at least a decade. Against 428 contemporaneous single transplants from high-KDPI donors, the dual recipients had better patient and graft survival and renal function, although death-censored graft survival was similar, and projected half-lives were 7.8 versus 5.9 years. Yearly dual activity fell from 9.0 to 2.7 and then 1.6 as US allocation rules changed. For UK units weighing whether to accept a marginal pair rather than decline both, the data suggest dual implantation into an older, low-risk recipient can provide durable function, provided the allocation framework makes it workable.

### 3. [Expanding transplant access via robotics: a multi-center American experience with 671 robotic kidney transplants.](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-026-04176-w)
[Abreu P, Kadri H, Alaniz J, Kiani A, Godfrey C, Vachharajani N, Schold JD, Pshak T, Khan AS, Spaggiari M. *J Robot Surg*, 2026. PMID: 43002268.]{.kw-ref}

Three US centres pooled every robotic kidney transplant from the start of their programmes to December 2025, a total of 671 procedures, with results broken down by recipient BMI, donor type and arterial anatomy. The case mix was dominated by obesity: 87.8% of recipients were obese and almost half (47.5%) morbidly so, and just over half (55.1%) received a living-donor kidney. Median operating time was 273 minutes and median warm ischaemia 44 minutes, and only 0.6% of cases were converted to open surgery. Delayed graft function (16.2%) and major complications (12.1%) did not vary with BMI, although delayed function ranged widely by donor type, from 2.2% with living donors to 48.3% with rapid-recovery DCD kidneys. Patient survival was 96.5%, 92.5% and 87.3% at one, three and five years, with graft survival of 96.9%, 93.4% and 86.8%, but recipients with a BMI of 40 or more had significantly worse patient survival. The study is retrospective and has no open-surgery comparator. For UK surgeons, it adds multicentre reassurance that the robotic approach is reproducible in recipients who might otherwise be turned down on weight, although patient survival was still lower in those with a BMI of 40 or more.

### 4. [Induction immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients treated with early corticosteroid cessation: A propensity score case-matched analysis.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajt.2026.10.029)
[Hendren E, Lan J, Kadatz M, Sridhar V, Avgay G, O'Donoghue D, Farkas V, Borg J, Rojas W, Gill JS. *Am J Transplant*, 2026. PMID: 43003189.]{.kw-ref}

This US registry analysis examined first kidney-only transplant recipients from 2010 to 2022 who were maintained on tacrolimus and mycophenolate with early steroid withdrawal. Only 13% of such patients had received an interleukin-2 receptor antagonist for induction rather than rabbit anti-thymocyte globulin, and those who did tended to be older and more often diabetic. After 1:1 propensity matching of 4,770 recipients, IL-2 receptor antagonist induction was associated with a 20% higher adjusted hazard of graft loss from any cause (HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.29). The same excess was seen for death with a functioning graft (HR 1.20, 1.10 to 1.31) and for graft loss when death was treated as a competing risk (subhazard ratio 1.20, 1.04 to 1.38). The authors acknowledge that the lighter induction was being chosen for frailer patients, so residual confounding cannot be excluded, and they call for a prospective trial. For UK units that combine basiliximab induction with steroid-sparing maintenance, this finding deserves attention at the next protocol review, although observational data alone are not enough to justify a switch to depleting induction.

### 5. [Peri-transplant eculizumab for preventing antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplant recipients at high immunologic risk: a systematic review with design-stratified evidence synthesis.](https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1982870)
[Liang C, Bao R, Yin S, Song T, Lin T. *Front Immunol*, 2026. PMID: 42978583.]{.kw-ref}

This PROSPERO-registered review searched seven bibliographic and trial-registry databases plus supplementary sources, with database searches closing on 10 June 2026 and registry searches on 20 August 2026, for eculizumab-containing prophylaxis in sensitised, DSA-positive or ABO-incompatible recipients. Thirty-one reports were found, 30 of them belonging to 14 studies or registry projects, and the evidence was stratified by design rather than pooled. The one randomised trial showed no difference: centrally adjudicated antibody-mediated rejection occurred in 5 of 51 patients in each arm (risk ratio 1.00, 95% CI 0.31 to 3.25). A historical-control comparison suggested a large reduction (2 of 26 versus 21 of 51; RR 0.19), but changes in era, plasma exchange and clinical management over the same period make it hard to interpret. An 80-patient single-arm study recorded three rejection episodes by week nine. With longer follow-up, neither graft survival nor kidney function showed a consistent advantage, and persistent DSA and chronic microvascular injury remained. As UK desensitisation programmes consider complement blockade, this review indicates that terminal complement inhibition does not yet have trial evidence of preventing rejection beyond standard desensitisation.

### 6. [Impact of Blood Transfusions After Kidney Transplantation on Clinical Outcomes and Broadness of Sensitisation.](https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.71068)
[Gerber SL, Diebold M, Hönger G, Wehmeier C, Wolff T, Mujagic E, Widmer C, Buser A, Schaub S. *HLA*, 2026. PMID: 42984328.]{.kw-ref}

The Basel group asked whether red-cell transfusion after transplantation provokes rejection or widens the recipient's HLA antibody repertoire. They studied 519 recipients on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone who had single-antigen bead testing both before transplantation and at one year, and analysed transfusion both as present or absent and by number of units. One-year rates of clinical rejection (19.7% versus 15.3%), combined clinical and subclinical rejection, T-cell-mediated rejection and antibody-mediated rejection did not differ significantly between transfused and non-transfused patients. More than five units was linked to more antibody-mediated rejection in the unadjusted analysis, but the signal disappeared after time-dependent Cox adjustment (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.59). De novo DSA appeared in 3.5% of transfused and 3.1% of non-transfused recipients, cPRA did not change differently between groups, and new antibodies against common class I antigens were rare (around 1% or less). The authors conclude that HLA-selected blood is not needed in this setting. For UK teams, this supports transfusing a recipient early after transplant when clinically needed rather than withholding blood out of concern about sensitisation, at least under standard triple therapy.

### 7. [Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and resistance in ESBL-producing Enterobacterales bloodstream infections among kidney transplant recipients.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13756-026-01799-4)
[Pérez-Nadales E, Ruiz-Arabi E, Riccucci D, Carratalà J, Paul M, Fernández-Ruiz M, Álvarez-Marín R, Carmona I, de Lucas EM, Rodríguez-Álvarez RJ, David MD, Steinke SM, Pierrotti LC, Machuca I, Oriol I, Rodríguez-Baño J, Martínez-Martínez L, Aguado JM, Torre-Cisneros J, Castón JJ, Gutiérrez-Gutiérrez B. *Antimicrob Resist Infect Control*, 2026. PMID: 43021318.]{.kw-ref}

Drawing on the multicentre INCREMENT-SOT cohort, this retrospective study looked at 323 kidney recipients with a single-organism bloodstream infection caused by ESBL-producing Enterobacterales. About half (49.5%) had taken co-trimoxazole as Pneumocystis prophylaxis in the preceding 30 days. Resistance to co-trimoxazole was already common overall (82.7%) but reached 91.3% in those on prophylaxis against 74.2% in those not on it. With inverse probability weighting, recent prophylaxis carried a relative risk of resistance of 1.18 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.37), and the estimate was borderline after further adjustment (1.16, 1.00 to 1.35). An exploratory tree analysis singled out lymphopenia: among lymphopenic patients on prophylaxis, 94.4% of isolates were resistant. Combined resistance to co-trimoxazole and ciprofloxacin affected 70.3% of patients and was more frequent with prophylaxis, but this did not survive adjustment. The design is observational and limited to patients who already had ESBL bacteraemia. For UK clinicians, the practical message is not to rely on co-trimoxazole as an oral step-down for an ESBL bloodstream infection in a recipient who is on, or recently finished, Pneumocystis prophylaxis.

### 8. [Post-donation systolic blood pressure trajectories after living kidney donation and paired recipient outcomes: a nationwide prospective cohort study from KOTRY.](https://doi.org/10.5646/ch.2026.32.e46)
[Yoon HE, Cheong HK, Choi SJN, Shin S, Han S, Yang J, Kim MS, Lee JY, Lee YH, Hwang HS. *Clin Hypertens*, 2026. PMID: 43010941.]{.kw-ref}

Investigators from the Korean Organ Transplantation Registry used latent class mixture modelling on serial post-donation blood pressure readings from 3,844 living donor-recipient pairs in this prospective, multicentre national cohort. Two linear trajectories emerged: a gradual rise in 95.1% of donors and a steeper rise in 4.9%. Donors in the steep group had a higher cumulative incidence of new hypertension, diabetes and eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (all p<0.001). Their recipients were also affected: among recipients who were normotensive before transplantation, a kidney from a steep-trajectory donor more than doubled the adjusted hazard of new hypertension (HR 2.70, 95% CI 1.44 to 5.08), with a graded relationship across the probability of steep-group membership. Among recipients with existing hypertension, donor trajectory was not linked to poor blood pressure control, but it was associated with a faster fall in eGFR (adjusted β −0.67). The authors interpret the donor's blood pressure course as a marker of risk shared by donor and recipient. For UK living-donor programmes, it argues for regular long-term blood pressure surveillance of donors, and for considering that a donor's rising pressure may also be relevant to the recipient's follow-up.
